statement: For the ordinary exterior algebra of a free rank-2n integral symplectic module, ξ^n=n!·vol; hence L^n:Λ^0→Λ^{2n} is not an integral isomorphism for n≥2. Ordinary contraction acts on L^j p by j(n−i−j+1)L^{j−1}p, whereas the draft’s endpoint relations prescribe unit-step lowering. Rationalizing resolves the first obstruction but not the second normalization mismatch.
reconstruction: The factorial and contraction tests are the earlier run’s exact counterchecks, not computations written by Grothendieck. Divided powers, other lattices, or normalized contraction are possible reconstructed models, not silent repairs of the source.
check_reason: The quoted integral assertion is present. The later endpoint relations determine a different lowering operator from ordinary contraction. The second pass changes the reference on scan 14 to 6.(5|15), so the old categorical quotation of (6.5) is no longer the current reading.

his_words: Il faut donc se donner en même temps L et les πᵢ; Non
statement: In the n=1 normalized Lefschetz algebra Mat₂(ℤ)×ℤ, conjugation by 1+tL fixes L but changes Λ and the degree projectors: gΛg⁻¹=Λ+t(π₂−π₀)−t²L. Thus specifying the raising operator alone does not specify the algebra map; the prescribed grading matters. The algebra has rank five.
reconstruction: The displayed conjugation family is supplied by the earlier run. The circled negative answer and five-element basis are on the page.
check_reason: The text retracts uniqueness from L alone and explicitly calls the projector condition essential. This is a resolved question within the pages, not an open modern conjecture.

statement: For a nonsingular symmetric integral matrix Q, the finite cokernel D_Q=ℤ^r/Qℤ^r has the perfect symmetric pairing xᵀQ⁻¹y mod ℤ. For Q=(−m), the value is −ab/m mod ℤ. Identifying a geometric Néron–Severi group with D_Q requires the local-surface hypotheses absent from the isolated sheet.
reconstruction: The formula and elementary proof are the earlier run’s explanation of the printed claim, not a formula printed on scan 19.
check_reason: The page asserts autoduality from the intersection matrix; the entry appropriately separates the elementary lattice statement from geometric identification.

statement: A point blowup changes Q to Q′=[[Q−vvᵀ,v],[vᵀ,−1]], integrally congruent to Q⊕(−1). The discriminant group and its pairing are unchanged. Resolution independence additionally uses common domination of resolutions in the stated surface setting.
reconstruction: The block congruence is the earlier run’s computation; geometric common domination is an explicit reconstructed prerequisite.
check_reason: The sheet asserts resolution independence, but its proof is not on the sheet. The entry provides only the blowup linear algebra.

his_words: idéaux maximaux ... homogènes; valeurs dans k
statement: The finite étale algebra 𝔽₂³ is not generated by one element over 𝔽₂: each element has at most two distinct coordinates. A nonzero polynomial over a finite field need not have a rational nonzero value. Consequently an unqualified monogenic/discriminant argument fails. No grading is supplied that makes “homogènes” a clear replacement for “principaux”.
reconstruction: The finite-field example is the earlier run’s counterexample. The alternative “principaux” is a mathematical reading proposal only; the second pass confirmed the ink “homogènes”.
check_reason: The notes correctly find two logically separate gaps: the finite-field argument and the unidentified adjective. They cannot be repaired merely by substituting the suggested word.

statement: For a smooth proper geometrically connected surface over an algebraically closed field and ℓ invertible, the rational Tate module of the cohomological Brauer group is the orthogonal complement of NS(X)⊗ℚℓ in H²(X,ℚℓ(1)). This is not a perfect pairing on the whole torsion Brauer group. The lattice induced on the quotient is integral and unimodular when ℓ does not divide the Néron–Severi discriminant; the finite ℓ-primary quotient is measured by torsion in H³(X,ℤℓ(1)).
reconstruction: The full surface and coefficient hypotheses are recovered from the published context, not all repeated on the two loose pages.
check_reason: The distinction between rational pairing, integral Tate lattice, and finite torsion quotient is required by the text’s exact sequences.

statement: The fragment concerns Matlis theory over a commutative noetherian ring: indecomposable injectives are injective hulls of residue fields at primes; localization identifies the appropriate local hull, and annihilator layers are dual to successive powers of the maximal ideal. Isomorphism classes and multiplicities are unique, not a canonical direct-sum splitting.
reconstruction: Identification with Matlis is bibliographical comparison. The surviving sheet does not give a full title or independent proof.
check_reason: The terminology, theorem number, and stated annihilator filtration match the cited primary article.

statement: For x∈X and an injective O_{X,x}-module I, the skyscraper-like direct image i_{x*}I is injective as an O_X-module, because Hom_X(F,i_{x*}I)=Hom_{O_{X,x}}(F_x,I) and the stalk functor is exact. In the noetherian affine setting the associated injective sheaf has this form; support is the closure of {x}.
reconstruction: The adjunction proof is the earlier run’s supplied proof. The global category and noetherian setting are retained.
check_reason: The page states injectivity among all O_X-modules. Restricting the assertion silently to quasi-coherent objects would weaken the actual text.

statement: The local surface identification NS(U)≅coker((C_i·C_j)) is to be read in the setting of a complete normal two-dimensional local ring, algebraically closed residue field, and a regular resolution that is an isomorphism away from the closed point. The isolated tail begins after these hypotheses.
reconstruction: These prerequisites are imported explicitly from Brauer III §8.4; the loose leaf itself does not state them.
check_reason: The note correctly flags that the determinant statement is not a theorem about an arbitrary punctured local scheme.

statement: The lattice discriminant pairing attached to a resolution and the pairing arising from local étale duality are different constructions whose compatibility needs a geometric comparison theorem. Constructing either pairing, or showing equal group orders, does not establish their equality.
reconstruction: The explicit warning “not verified” is found in published Brauer III, Remark 8.5, rather than on the isolated scan 19; the item’s self-flagged status therefore has a published-text locator.
check_reason: The entry does not confuse the elementary pairing with the unresolved comparison. A later paper on surface duality alone is not an exact settlement.

statement: Mumford’s negative-definiteness theorem for exceptional curves supports nonsingularity of the intersection matrix in the appropriate resolution setting. His topological calculation supports an analogous discriminant group, but is not itself a proof of every ℓ-adic pairing comparison in Grothendieck’s local algebraic setting.
reconstruction: The separation of topological and étale conclusions is an editorial scope check.
check_reason: The note accurately prevents a single citation from carrying a stronger compatibility conclusion than its stated result.

his_words: premier idéal de Filting; A^p → A^q
statement: For a finitely presented module with q generators, Fitt₀(M)⊂Ann(M) and Ann(M)^q⊂Fitt₀(M). The Kähler different of B/A is Fitt₀^B(Ω_{B/A}); the presentation used to compute it must be over B. “Premier” in this passage corresponds to modern Fitt₀ notation.
reconstruction: Modern indexing and the B-linear correction are editorial explanations. The typed spelling and coefficient A are preserved as source readings.
check_reason: Both the index and coefficient ring matter. The second pass confirms the literal A and “Filting”, so mathematical corrections must not be presented as new transcriptions.

statement: For composable finite flat complete-intersection algebras, block-triangular Jacobian presentations give multiplicativity of the different: D_{C/A}=D_{C/B}·D_{B/A}C. A determinant calculation proves this under its presentation hypotheses; the fragment does not state a universal formula for arbitrary maps.
reconstruction: The two-equation determinant model is the earlier run’s test, not a proof of the unrestricted word “transitivité”.
check_reason: The note preserves rather than suppresses the complete-intersection hypotheses.

statement: Comparison of the Kähler different with the trace/Dedekind different requires finite generically separable algebras and, for the clean equality, a locally complete-intersection (in particular appropriate finite DVR) setting. In inseparable fraction-field extensions the trace pairing is degenerate.
reconstruction: The separability and finiteness qualifications are a modern reconstruction of the applicable theorem, not ink inserted into the draft.
check_reason: The note correctly asks which hypotheses govern the comparison.

his_words: Algèbres étales sur A → Algèbres étales sur A/I
statement: For a nilpotent ideal I⊂A, reduction induces an equivalence between the categories of étale A-algebras and étale A/I-algebras, and between their finite étale subcategories. This includes morphisms and uniqueness up to unique lift, not only a bijection of isomorphism classes.
reconstruction: The full categorical formulation is standard and makes explicit the arrow on the page.
check_reason: The fragment states an equivalence, and the entry retains its categorical strength.

statement: Coherence/quasi-coherence of RHom(L,M) holds with L bounded above and coherent and M bounded below with the corresponding finiteness, or with the stated bounded-below L and uniform finite Ext-dimension alternative. It is false with arbitrary unbounded inputs: over a field, zero-differential complexes having one copy of k in every nonnegative degree give H⁰RHom=∏_{i≥0}k, not a finite-dimensional vector space.
reconstruction: The infinite-product counterexample is the earlier run’s test. It refutes an extension without boundedness, not the qualified proposition printed on the page.
check_reason: Both boundedness alternatives are present and must be retained. The finite Ext-dimension alternative is not redundant.

Bottom-string projectors are obtained by differences of eΛ^rL^re, e=1−LΛ; matrix units are L^b e_i Λ^a.

statement: For a finite graded ring or faithful graded module with homogeneous inverse pairs for each complementary Lefschetz degree, the degree projectors can be recovered by induction. Statements require finite support, prescribed degree bounds, homogeneous maps and both inverse identities. A proof that uses a global identity operator must include source and target cutoffs.

statement: Hard Lefschetz is a cohomological isomorphism theorem. Algebraicity of its inverse, or of normalized lowering, is the additional standard conjecture B. Deligne’s hard-Lefschetz theorem does not settle that algebraicity question in general.
reconstruction: Modern terminology and subsequent theorem attribution are external commentary, not part of the 1960s text.
check_reason: The note correctly separates linear invertibility from realization by algebraic cycles.

statement: On a normalized Lefschetz string L kills the top and Λ kills the bottom; LΛ is identity away from the bottom and ΛL away from the top. Cancelled versions of these formulas cannot be counted as final assertions; the live endpoint equations on scan 14 govern the later formulas.

statement: For a smooth hyperplane Y⊂X and a Weil cohomology satisfying hard and weak Lefschetz, algebraicity of lowering on X is equivalent to the corresponding property on Y together with the appropriate algebraic-cycle Lefschetz condition on X×Y (or X×X). Iterating along a smooth flag gives a universal implication from the collection of A-properties to B. This is not the pointwise implication A(X)⇒B(X).
reconstruction: Letters are translated operationally; twists and degree bounds are supplied explicitly in the claim records. The equivalence is a theorem about the conjunction, not a proof that the conjectures hold.
check_reason: The note correctly emphasizes quantifiers, hyperplane hypotheses, and the necessary product variety.

statement: The weakened hyperplane conditions use a mixture of codimension inequalities and cohomology-degree labels. A precise claim requires fixing whether i indexes cycles or H^i and then checking all Gysin shifts. The displayed factorization has degree +4 in even dimension and +2 in odd dimension; the unresolved local inequalities cannot be silently replaced.

statement: If v=L^{n−i}:H^i→H^{2n−i} is invertible and some algebraic u:H^{2n−i}→H^i is invertible, and uv has a rational characteristic polynomial with nonzero constant term, Cayley–Hamilton gives v⁻¹=(uv)⁻¹u as a rational polynomial correspondence. Algebraic isomorphisms do not supply their inverse without the polynomial-coefficient hypothesis or another argument.
reconstruction: The unambiguous order (uv)⁻¹u is a modern typed reconstruction of the proof, whose local operator letters are uncertain.
check_reason: The note correctly isolates the finite-dimensional algebra argument and its rationality hypothesis.

statement: The author retracts a claim of independence of positive-characteristic standard conjectures from the chosen Weil cohomology. Independence from polarization is a separate, established formal theorem and does not establish independence from cohomology theory.
reconstruction: The modern separation of the two parameters is editorial; the retraction and request for a proof are explicit.
check_reason: The retraction must survive consolidation. Neither finite-field Künneth projectors nor polarization independence settles the broad retracted statement.

statement: Let A be a finite-dimensional rational algebra with a positive involutive trace form Tr(a*a)>0 for nonzero a. Its Jacobson radical is zero: the involution preserves the radical, a*a is radical and nilpotent, hence has trace zero. Applying this to correspondences requires the relevant algebraicity and index hypotheses and a justified finite-dimensional rational algebra.
reconstruction: The radical proof is the earlier run’s explanation of the conditional assertion. Mere inclusion of a Q-algebra in a finite-dimensional Qℓ-space does not prove finite Q-dimension.
check_reason: The note supplies the missing rational-finiteness qualification rather than treating positivity as an unconditional geometric theorem.

statement: In a semisimple category of the relevant algebraic correspondences, monomorphisms and epimorphisms split. A positivity argument on End(H*(X)) alone does not justify an algebraic splitting for a map X→X′; the ambient category or the endomorphism algebra of X⊕X′ must satisfy the corresponding hypotheses.
reconstruction: The ambient direct-sum requirement is an editorial completion of the conditional argument, not a hypothesis printed in full on the loose page.
check_reason: The note correctly resists promoting arbitrary linear splittings to algebraic correspondences.

statement: Jannsen proves semisimplicity for pure numerical motives with characteristic-zero coefficients. This does not unconditionally prove semisimplicity for homological motives. Under algebraic Künneth projectors a homological-to-numerical kernel can be a nilpotent radical, which is weaker than vanishing of that radical.
reconstruction: Both comparisons concern later literature; neither theorem is written on this manuscript page.
check_reason: The two notes address the same dangerous overidentification and are consolidated with the distinction explicit.

statement: Over finite fields, Katz–Messing provides algebraic rational Künneth projectors and characteristic-polynomial comparisons for algebraic correspondences in the specified cohomology theories. These results address that finite-field setting and do not prove the full Lefschetz standard conjecture over every field.
reconstruction: Entirely a later-literature comparison. Its exact theorem scope is checked in the primary paper.
check_reason: The note’s scope is appropriately narrower than the retracted universal independence assertion.

statement: For the displayed graded-commutative algebra H⁰=k,H¹=V,H²=kξ⊕W,H³=V∨,H⁴=kξ², associativity imposes the boxed quadratic identity on φ, ψ and Q. Nondegeneracy of alternating φ and symmetric Q controls Lefschetz and duality, but does not imply that associativity identity. The two-dimensional symplectic example with W=0 violates associativity.

statement: Over a field of characteristic different from two, take the orthogonal space kξ⊕kw with Q(ξ,ξ)=1,Q(w,w)=−1, and send x∧y to φ(x,y)(ξ+w), where φ is symplectic. Its image is an isotropic line not contained in W, so the induced four-form χ is zero while the Lefschetz alternating form is nondegenerate.

Its six-dimensional rational model and varying-dimensional family can then test infinite forward orbits and unbounded cyclic dimensions. These calculations establish only that explicit normalization and the stated families; they do not decide the manuscript’s unresolved W/V parenthesis or its proposed dimension-four threshold.
